extracted.intended_audience: AAAI-24 authors and reviewers (conference paper submitters and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing submission, anonymization, reviewing phases, author responses, and reviewer responsibilities for the AAAI-24 conference. Applies to authors preparing submissions and reviewers writing evaluations for AAAI-24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1: Initial allocation and early rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every paper will be allocated two reviewers. If a paper receives two reviews that are both sufficiently negative, it will be rejected without any opportunity for author feedback."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 assigns two reviewers per paper; if both reviews are 'sufficiently negative' the paper is rejected immediately with no author response opportunity. Authors and reviewers should understand that strong early negative consensus can lead to outright rejection before Phase 2 or author feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2: Additional reviewers and blind separation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each paper will be allocated additional reviewers. These reviewers will not be given access to Phase 1 reviews until after submitting their own reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 2 brings extra reviewers who must form independent judgments without seeing Phase 1 text, reducing anchoring and bias. Reviewers in Phase 2 submit their reports before viewing Phase 1 reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author feedback / unified author response window
rubrics_metrics.description: A unified feedback opportunity permits Phase 2 authors to respond to all evaluations from both phases between November 2-5, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors have a specified short window (Nov 2–5, 2023) to respond to reviews from both phases; program committee deliberations will incorporate these author responses after the window. Authors should prepare concise, focused responses that address reviewer concerns within the allotted timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: "AAAI-24 reviews are double blind (i.e., neither reviewers nor authors should be able to identify each other). Papers must exclude author names, affiliations, and identifying acknowledgments from initial pages."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must remove identifying metadata (author names, affiliations, acknowledgments) from the initial submission. Both authors and reviewers are expected to avoid actions that would compromise anonymity. Follow the conference's double-blind procedures strictly to preserve review integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation practices under double-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should reference prior work using third-person attribution rather than first-person claims. Anonymous citations are permissible when appropriate. "Preprint versions on platforms like arXiv do not violate blind review policies if submissions do not reference this material."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing your own previous work, use third-person phrasing (e.g., 'Prior work [X] showed...') or anonymous citation practices if necessary to avoid revealing authorship. Be cautious about referencing publicly posted preprints that could identify authors; posting preprints is not itself a violation, but submissions should avoid explicit references that reveal identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to ethical guidelines and malpractice policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The document references "Ethical Guidelines for AAAI-24 Reviewers" and a "Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers must follow the conference's ethical guidelines and malpractice policies (e.g., conflicts of interest, confidentiality, plagiarism). Although full details are not given in the excerpt, participants should consult and comply with the linked Ethical Guidelines and Publications Ethics statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibility and permitted use of tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are fully responsible for the entire content of their reviews. Tools can be used to improve the wording of the review but not to generate its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must ensure the substantive judgments, evaluations, and content of their reviews are their own. Using external tools (e.g., language-editing aids) is allowed only for wording/clarity; reviewers must not use tools to produce the review's substantive content or evaluations.
